query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has been focused on understanding their unique properties, such as high strength, ductility, and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. Earlier studies have explored the effects of grain-boundary segregation, brittle grain-boundary precipitation, and rapid grain coarsening on the mechanical properties of these alloys. Recent studies have investigated the deformation mechanisms, dislocation structures, and grain boundary decohesion in high-entropy alloys. The trend suggests a shift towards understanding the underlying mechanisms governing the toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys, with a focus on the role of grain boundaries, dislocations, and nanoclustering.
decision.unsolved: The exact mechanisms governing toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys, particularly the role of grain boundaries, dislocations, and nanoclustering, remain unclear. The relationship between grain boundary decohesion, nanoclustering, and toughness degradation is not well understood. Additionally, the effects of temperature, loading, and composition on the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys require further investigation.
decision.why: To investigate the nanoscale mechanisms governing toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys, atom probe tomography can be used to study the grain boundary decohesion, nanoclustering, and dislocation structures in these alloys. This technique can provide detailed information on the atomic-scale distribution of elements and defects, allowing for a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms governing toughness degradation.
